name: RF separator
description: Identical particles, one launched half an RF period after the other. No static field can tell them apart; an oscillating one can. RF separators at CERN sorted kaons from pions this way. Send each bunch to its own detector.

reality.represents: An RF separator, as at CERN for kaons and pions

remarks.detail: Particles that reach an oscillating field at different phases are kicked differently, which no static field can do.

Real separators sort particles of equal momentum but different mass: after a long drift their different speeds bring them to the deflecting cavities at different phases. Here two identical particles leave half a period apart.
Each antenna is an oscillating point dipole with its exact retarded fields (near, induction and radiation zones); real RF deflectors are resonant cavities or plates driven by a generator.

c is a few cells per time unit, so that the board spans less than a wavelength of the RF and the particle crosses it in a few periods; the physics depends only on such ratios (v/c, the wavelength against the board), which real devices share.
